fruits.extendedStory: Building began in 1458, to a design attributed to Filippo Brunelleschi. The style is Renaissance, which prized balance and clear straight proportion over decoration. For centuries this was a private house, shut to everyone outside it. The doors opened to the public in 1919, and the rooms behind them have stayed open ever since.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Bau begann 1458, nach einem Entwurf, der Filippo Brunelleschi zugeschrieben wird. Der Stil ist Renaissance, der Gleichmaß und klare gerade Verhältnisse über allen Schmuck stellte. Jahrhundertelang war dies ein privates Haus, verschlossen für alle von draußen. 1919 öffneten sich die Türen für alle, und seither stehen die Räume dahinter offen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Building began in 1458, to a design attributed to Filippo Brunelleschi. The style is Renaissance, which prized balance and clear straight proportion over decoration. For centuries this was a private house, shut to everyone outside it. The doors opened to the public in 1919, and the rooms behind them have stayed open ever since.

localizedStory.de: Filippo Brunelleschi gestaltete diesen Renaissance-Palast, begonnen 1458.
localizedStory.en: Filippo Brunelleschi shaped this Renaissance palace, begun in 1458.

fruits.name: Palazzo Pitti
fruits.story: Filippo Brunelleschi shaped this Renaissance palace, begun in 1458.

fruits.extendedStory: Two dates cling to this crossing, 1335 and 1345, and the records do not agree which is right. What is certain is that Neri di Fioravante is the man credited with the work. The bridge has stood on its stone arches through every flood and every century since. Cross it slowly and you are walking a road Florence has used for close to seven hundred years.

localizedExtendedStory.de: An diesem Übergang haften zwei Jahreszahlen, 1335 und 1345, und die Quellen sind sich nicht einig. Sicher ist, dass Neri di Fioravante als sein Baumeister gilt. Auf seinen steinernen Bögen steht er seither durch jedes Hochwasser und jedes Jahrhundert. Wer langsam hinübergeht, benutzt eine Straße, die Florenz seit fast siebenhundert Jahren dient.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Two dates cling to this crossing, 1335 and 1345, and the records do not agree which is right. What is certain is that Neri di Fioravante is the man credited with the work. The bridge has stood on its stone arches through every flood and every century since. Cross it slowly and you are walking a road Florence has used for close to seven hundred years.

localizedStory.de: Neri di Fioravante spannte diesen Übergang 1345 über den Arno, und er trägt Florenz seither.
localizedStory.en: Neri di Fioravante threw this crossing over the Arno in 1345, and it has carried Florence ever since.

fruits.name: Ponte Vecchio
fruits.story: Neri di Fioravante threw this crossing over the Arno in 1345, and it has carried Florence ever since.

fruits.extendedStory: Look downstream and the view runs over the Uffizi, the Vasari Corridor and the Ponte Vecchio. Then look at the ground under your feet. Medieval and Renaissance Florence had no riverside walk here at all. This embankment belongs to the 1865 plan of Giuseppe Poggi, drawn up when the city was the capital of Italy.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Blick flussabwärts, und der Blick läuft über die Uffizien, den Vasarikorridor und den Ponte Vecchio. Dann schau auf den Boden unter deinen Füßen. Das mittelalterliche und das Renaissance-Florenz hatten hier gar keinen Uferweg. Diese Promenade gehört zum Plan von Giuseppe Poggi aus dem Jahr 1865, entworfen, als die Stadt Hauptstadt Italiens war.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Look downstream and the view runs over the Uffizi, the Vasari Corridor and the Ponte Vecchio. Then look at the ground under your feet. Medieval and Renaissance Florence had no riverside walk here at all. This embankment belongs to the 1865 plan of Giuseppe Poggi, drawn up when the city was the capital of Italy.

localizedStory.de: Dieser Blick über den Arno zeigt die moderne Stadt, die nach Giuseppe Poggis Plan von 1865 angelegt wurde.
localizedStory.en: This Arno viewpoint looks out on the modern city laid out under Giuseppe Poggi's 1865 plan.

fruits.name: Belvedere sull'Arno
fruits.story: This Arno viewpoint looks out on the modern city laid out under Giuseppe Poggi's 1865 plan.

fruits.extendedStory: Work started in 1298, and the tower is credited to Arnolfo di Cambio. It is Gothic, which means tall pointed shapes and windows that reach upward rather than sitting square. At 84.7 metres it climbs well clear of the roofs around it. From the foot you cannot take it all in at once, so step back into Piazza del Duomo.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Arbeiten begannen 1298, und der Turm wird Arnolfo di Cambio zugeschrieben. Er ist gotisch, also voller hoher spitzer Formen und Fenster, die nach oben streben statt eckig dazusitzen. Mit 84,7 Metern ragt er weit über die Dächer ringsum. Vom Fuß aus bekommt man ihn nicht ganz ins Auge, also tritt zurück auf die Piazza del Duomo.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Work started in 1298, and the tower is credited to Arnolfo di Cambio. It is Gothic, which means tall pointed shapes and windows that reach upward rather than sitting square. At 84.7 metres it climbs well clear of the roofs around it. From the foot you cannot take it all in at once, so step back into Piazza del Duomo.

localizedStory.de: Dieser gotische Glockenturm steigt 84,7 Meter neben dem Dom auf, begonnen 1298.
localizedStory.en: This Gothic bell tower climbs 84.7 metres beside the cathedral, begun in 1298.

fruits.name: Campanile di Giotto
fruits.story: This Gothic bell tower climbs 84.7 metres beside the cathedral, begun in 1298.

fruits.extendedStory: From 1563 this square hosted the Palio dei Cocchi, a Roman-style chariot race set up by Cosimo I de' Medici. Two marble obelisks marked the turning-posts where the carts swung round. Each rests on four bronze tortoises made by Giambologna. Both obelisks still stand on the square today.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Ab 1563 fand auf diesem Platz das Palio dei Cocchi statt, ein Wagenrennen im römischen Stil, das Cosimo I. de' Medici einführte. Zwei Marmor-Obelisken markierten die Wendepunkte, um die die Wagen herumfuhren. Jeder ruht auf vier Bronze-Schildkröten, die Giambologna schuf. Beide Obelisken stehen bis heute auf dem Platz.
localizedExtendedStory.en: From 1563 this square hosted the Palio dei Cocchi, a Roman-style chariot race set up by Cosimo I de' Medici. Two marble obelisks marked the turning-posts where the carts swung round. Each rests on four bronze tortoises made by Giambologna. Both obelisks still stand on the square today.

localizedStory.de: Such nach vier bronzenen Schildkröten von Giambologna, die zwei Marmor-Obelisken tragen, einst die Wendepunkte eines Wagenrennens.
localizedStory.en: Look for four bronze tortoises by Giambologna carrying two marble obelisks that once marked a chariot race.

fruits.name: Piazza Santa Maria Novella
fruits.story: Look for four bronze tortoises by Giambologna carrying two marble obelisks that once marked a chariot race.

fruits.extendedStory: The church took a very long time to finish. Arnolfo di Cambio laid it out in 1294, but it was not opened until 1442, nearly a hundred and fifty years later. Generations of masons worked on a building none of them would ever see completed. Its name, Santa Croce, means the True Cross.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Kirche brauchte sehr lange bis zur Vollendung. Arnolfo di Cambio legte sie 1294 an, eröffnet wurde sie aber erst 1442, fast hundertfünfzig Jahre später. Ganze Generationen von Steinmetzen arbeiteten an einem Bau, den keiner von ihnen fertig sah. Ihr Name, Santa Croce, bedeutet Wahres Kreuz.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The church took a very long time to finish. Arnolfo di Cambio laid it out in 1294, but it was not opened until 1442, nearly a hundred and fifty years later. Generations of masons worked on a building none of them would ever see completed. Its name, Santa Croce, means the True Cross.

localizedStory.de: Arnolfo di Cambio begann diese gotische Kirche 1294; ihr Name bedeutet Wahres Kreuz.
localizedStory.en: Arnolfo di Cambio began this Gothic church in 1294; its name means the True Cross.

fruits.name: Basilica di Santa Croce
fruits.story: Arnolfo di Cambio began this Gothic church in 1294; its name means the True Cross.

fruits.extendedStory: This gallery opened in 1784 as a place to study art. Since 1873 it has sheltered Michelangelo's original marble David, moved here from Piazza della Signoria for safekeeping. The carved statue rises 5.17 metres tall from the floor. Visitors gather beneath it to look up at the great marble giant.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Diese Galerie wurde 1784 eröffnet, als Ort zum Studium der Kunst. Seit 1873 bewahrt sie Michelangelos originalen David aus Marmor, zur sicheren Aufbewahrung hergebracht von der Piazza della Signoria. Die gemeißelte Figur ragt 5,17 Meter vom Boden auf. Besucher versammeln sich darunter und blicken zu dem steinernen Riesen hinauf.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This gallery opened in 1784 as a place to study art. Since 1873 it has sheltered Michelangelo's original marble David, moved here from Piazza della Signoria for safekeeping. The carved statue rises 5.17 metres tall from the floor. Visitors gather beneath it to look up at the great marble giant.

localizedStory.de: Drinnen steht Michelangelos echter David aus Marmor, 5,17 Meter hoch.
localizedStory.en: Inside stands Michelangelo's real marble David, 5.17 metres of carved marble.

fruits.name: Galleria dell'Accademia
fruits.story: Inside stands Michelangelo's real marble David, 5.17 metres of carved marble.

fruits.extendedStory: The square takes its name from the Signoria of Florence, the city's old government. Set into the stone is a round plaque that marks one exact spot. It remembers the friar Girolamo Savonarola and the year 1498. Every year the city gathers there and covers the plaque with flowers, in a ceremony called the Fiorita.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Platz trägt seinen Namen nach der Signoria von Florenz, der alten Stadtregierung. In den Steinboden ist eine runde Platte eingelassen, die genau eine Stelle markiert. Sie erinnert an den Mönch Girolamo Savonarola und an das Jahr 1498. Jedes Jahr versammelt sich die Stadt dort und bedeckt die Platte mit Blumen, bei einer Zeremonie namens Fiorita.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The square takes its name from the Signoria of Florence, the city's old government. Set into the stone is a round plaque that marks one exact spot. It remembers the friar Girolamo Savonarola and the year 1498. Every year the city gathers there and covers the plaque with flowers, in a ceremony called the Fiorita.

localizedStory.de: Eine originalgroße Kopie von Michelangelos David steht genau dort, wo das Original bis 1873 stand.
localizedStory.en: A full-size copy of Michelangelo's David marks the very spot where the original stood until 1873.

fruits.name: Piazza della Signoria
fruits.story: A full-size copy of Michelangelo's David marks the very spot where the original stood until 1873.
